findings.problem: The backend locator ignores binding decision D8. D8 says: NULL server means the backend picked by env RADIOS_AUDIO_BACKEND (wasapi default, virtual, none); the explicit strings "virtual:" and "none:" are honoured; the old "unix:/nonexistent..." literal maps to none. CTest sets RADIOS_AUDIO_BACKEND=none globally so that no test touches real devices. radios_audio_server_resolve() reads RADIOS_AUDIO_SERVER instead, knows only "wasapi", and returns a gboolean, so it cannot express none or virtual. The none safety net therefore does not exist: every realtime engine created under CTest (test_audio realtime cases, GUI tests, the hardware test harness) opens WASAPI and puts MAIN on "@default". On the user's PC that is the real default output (DDJ-FLX10, with rekordbox running). The implementer also recommends that patchbay.c and channel_input.c adopt this boolean resolver, which would carry the gap into the routing phase and leave the c-audio-virtual area no hook to plug into.
findings.evidence: Probe /opt/radios-port/work/review-wasapi-audio/probe_engine.c, run under Wine with RADIOS_AUDIO_BACKEND=none and server NULL, prints: connected=1, MAIN error 'Windows'ta varsayılan çıkış aygıtı yok...'. The engine went to WASAPI and tried to open the default endpoint; under Wine it found none. Code: wasapi_backend.c:1006 `g_getenv("RADIOS_AUDIO_SERVER")`; :1008 accepts only wasapi/wasapi:; everything else goes to backend_new(..., NULL ops, "Bu ses sunucusu adresi Windows'ta desteklenmiyor: %s"). tests/test_wasapi_backend.c:784-788 asserts the RADIOS_AUDIO_SERVER semantics and treats unix:/tmp/pulse as 'unsupported' rather than none.
findings.fix: Replace the boolean resolver with an enum: `typedef enum { RADIOS_AUDIO_BACKEND_KIND_WASAPI, _VIRTUAL, _NONE, _INVALID } RadioSAudioBackendKind; RadioSAudioBackendKind radios_audio_backend_resolve(const gchar *server, gchar error[256]);`. Order: explicit server first; else g_getenv("RADIOS_AUDIO_BACKEND"); else wasapi. Map "none"/"none:" and any "unix:" string to NONE (connected=FALSE, all buses not ready, one stable Turkish text). Map "virtual"/"virtual:" to a provider hook the c-audio-virtual area fills in (until then, NONE with its own text). Optionally keep RADIOS_AUDIO_SERVER as a deprecated alias. Update audio.h and audio_internal.h docs and the test: make the hardware harness and test_engine_realtime pass "wasapi:" explicitly so they still work under CTest's global none, and assert that RADIOS_AUDIO_BACKEND=none with server NULL never creates a WASAPI provider. Make radios_audio_backend_display_name()/label() report the backend actually in use.

findings.line: 636-663 (stall detection at 34 STALL_US, 38 REOPEN_WINDOW_US, 713-715; same window logic in mic_main 794-805)
findings.problem: A permanently stalled render stream is never escalated to an error. The watchdog only fires after 2 s without a device event (STALL_US), and an open plus the 2 s wait always takes longer than 2 s. The 'REOPEN_LIMIT within REOPEN_WINDOW_US (2 s)' counter therefore resets on every stall (now - reopen_window > 2 s), and the bus reopens silently forever. The Turkish TEXT_STALLED 'Ses aygıtı yanıt vermiyor' error is never published. The engine never sees a loss (ready stays TRUE except for a few ms per reopen, and there is never an error text). Automation freezes because played_tag and consumed_frames stop advancing. Result on a hung driver or USB interface: dead air with no operator alarm, which is not acceptable for broadcast. The implementer's report claims 'After that it becomes a loss with a Turkish reason'.
findings.evidence: Probe /opt/radios-port/work/review-wasapi-audio/probe_core.c, case 'stall'. It drives the real backend core through radios_audio_backend_new_with_provider with a fake device whose started stream never signals or consumes. Output under Wine: 'T1 stall: initially ready=1, opens in 14 s=7, error ever reported=0 (), not-ready polls 0/2694, consumed now 0'. That is 7 silent reopens in 14 s, no error, and the snapshot never even showed ready=FALSE.
findings.fix: Count consecutive reopens without progress instead of using a 2 s wall-clock window. Reset reopen_attempts only after a reopened stream has really played, for example IAudioClock position advanced by at least 1 s, or 10 s of continuous good events. On the 2nd consecutive stall with no position progress, and once a REOPEN storm reaches REOPEN_LIMIT, publish PHASE_FAILED with TEXT_STALLED. The engine then pauses decks and shows the reason, and the 5 s route retry keeps trying. Apply the same rule to the mic path. Add a fake-provider regression test in which a stalling stream must produce a bus_error within about 10 s.

findings.problem: After every in-place flush, the refill ends as soon as 480 real frames are queued (REFILL_FRAMES). In the same bus_render pass, the low-water rule then pads silence up to 2 device periods before Start. If the engine has rendered only its first 480-frame block when the 1 ms refill poll runs, the device receives real audio, then (2*period - 480) frames of silence, then real audio. That is a 10 ms hole at the common 10 ms period, and larger on endpoints with longer periods, in the middle of the on-air deck after every seek, cue or stop of another deck. This regresses the Linux 'flush-keeps-other-deck-continuous' strict ≤480-frame gap contract documented in docs/kilavuz-2026-10-18-C.md. The hole is also invisible to the new gap_frames diagnostic, because silence written while !started is not counted; conversely, start-up silence written after Start but before the engine's first block is counted as a 'gap'. The code comment ('never while refilling after a flush, so no silence is queued ahead of fresh audio') and the report's 'industrial fix' claim do not hold.
findings.evidence: Probe /opt/radios-port/work/review-wasapi-audio/probe_core.c, case 'flush'. The fake device logs every write as real or silent per Reset epoch, and an engine-like producer renders 480-frame tagged blocks while the ring holds fewer than 4 blocks. With 0 µs render time per block: 0/40 flushes affected. With 400 µs per block: 'epochs with silence inserted between real audio after refill=37' of 40, all kept ready, gap_frames=0.
findings.fix: While the stream is not started after a flush, keep writing only real ring audio. End the refill only when the queued real audio is at least MAX(REFILL_FRAMES, low_water) or REFILL_TIMEOUT has expired. Never pad silence before the first Start of a refill unless that timeout expired. The engine renders 4 blocks right after a flush, so the threshold is reached within about 1-2 ms. Count gap_frames only for silence queued after the first real frame of a stream generation, before and after Start alike. Add a fake-provider test that asserts no silent write occurs between real writes after a flush.

findings.problem: Without hardware, the tests cover only device-list publishing, hotplug debounce, snapshot latency, service loss and the locator. fake_open always returns FAILED, so the whole bus state machine has zero coverage on CI or under Wine: render accounting and played_tag/consumed_frames, the 44.1 kHz resampler tag mapping, the in-place flush handshake and refill rule, REOPEN/stall handling, route retry and re-apply after reconnect. The cases spec audio-backend.md 6.3(a) requires are missing: route retry after 5 s; flush keeps a READY bus ready and resets counters; flush of a stalled bus returns within about 100 ms with ready=FALSE. The two defects above live exactly in that untested code, and the hardware cases on the PC would not catch them reliably.
findings.evidence: Ran the test under Wine 5 times plus once with G_DEBUG=fatal-warnings: 7 passed, 9 skipped every time. My fake playing provider in probe_core.c (about 100 lines) exercises those paths deterministically and exposed both defects within minutes.
findings.fix: Extend the fake provider with a playing stream: a clock that consumes written frames at the stream rate, padding, a period event, position, start/stop/reset, and switchable stall and invalidation. Add cases for played_tag monotonic and below the written tag; consumed ≈ elapsed; 44.1 kHz tags; flush keeps READY with consumed reset and no silence between real audio; flush of a blocked bus returns within 150 ms; stall escalates to an error; REOPEN storm escalates; route retry ≤5 s; reconnect re-applies buses.

findings.problem: The hardware-labelled variant (RADIOS_TEST_WASAPI=1) exits 0 when no render endpoint exists. It reruns the 7 software cases and skips the 9 hardware cases individually, so CTest reports the hardware test as Passed on machines without devices. ENV_CLOUD requires hardware-bound tests to skip cleanly with exit 77, and a 'Passed' hardware result could be mistaken for real-device verification.
findings.evidence: `RADIOS_TEST_WASAPI=1 wrun ./test_wasapi_backend.exe` under Wine: cases 3-6 and 12-16 show '# SKIP', exit=0.
findings.fix: When RADIOS_TEST_WASAPI=1 is set but `hardware` is FALSE, print the reason and return 77 before g_test_run. Alternatively, split the hardware cases into their own executable or test path that returns 77, and register SKIP_RETURN_CODE 77.

findings.problem: The hardware cases treat AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_IN_USE as a test failure. The microphone case skips only on the privacy text or 'no default input'; layer_tone and backend_tone assert RADIOS_WASAPI_OK / ready on "@default". The user's default endpoints belong to the DDJ-FLX10 driven by rekordbox, so if rekordbox (or any DAW) takes the endpoint in exclusive mode, the suite fails on the PC for an environmental reason, not a defect.
findings.evidence: Code reading: test_microphone asserts `strstr(error, "Mikrofon izni kapalı") || strstr(error, "varsayılan giriş")`; the TEXT_IN_USE message ('Aygıt başka bir uygulamanın özel kullanımında...') fails that assertion.
findings.fix: Treat RADIOS_WASAPI_FAILED with radios_wasapi_stream_hresult()==AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_IN_USE (0x8889000A) as g_test_skip("device held exclusively by another application") in the layer cases, and skip the backend cases when bus_error contains the in-use text.

findings.problem: The power-throttling opt-out ignores the result of SetProcessInformation and combines EXECUTION_SPEED with IGNORE_TIMER_RESOLUTION (0x4) in one call. Microsoft documents IGNORE_TIMER_RESOLUTION only for the Windows 11 behaviour, and older Windows 10 builds may reject the unknown ControlMask bit. If they do, the EcoQoS/LowQoS opt-out is silently lost too, and nothing is logged.
findings.evidence: Code reading against the SetProcessInformation and PROCESS_POWER_THROTTLING_STATE documentation (learn.microsoft.com). The struct page lists only EXECUTION_SPEED; IGNORE_TIMER_RESOLUTION is described in the context of Windows 11 behaviour. PLAUSIBLE: neither Wine nor the user's Windows 11 PC can show the Windows 10 behaviour.
findings.fix: Check the BOOL result. On failure, retry with ControlMask = PROCESS_POWER_THROTTLING_EXECUTION_SPEED alone, and log once with g_debug or g_message.

findings.problem: When Windows refuses AUTOCONVERTPCM, the mix-format fallback is used only if the mix rate equals the requested rate; otherwise the stream fails with the 'format' text. Backend spec 5.6.5 (capture: resample to 48 kHz with an any-rate resampler) and routing spec 5.6 (retry with the mix format and swresample to 48 k) both require resampling in that case. This is a small gap in the shared layer the routing phase will build on.
findings.evidence: Code: `if (!attempt->convert && (!mix.usable || mix.rate != stream->rate)) continue;`. Not reproducible here: there are no endpoints under Wine, and AUTOCONVERTPCM is normally accepted on Windows 10 and 11.
findings.fix: For capture kinds, allow the mix-rate fallback and convert to spec->rate inside the layer with libswresample (or an any-rate radios_output_resampler constructor). Report info.rate honestly for render.

Windows review against Microsoft documentation: COM refcounts of the IMMNotificationClient and the agile activation handler; per-thread MTA (CoInitializeEx/CoUninitialize pairing); every COM object released on its owning thread; no device call under backend->lock; snapshot bounded; flush wait bounded at 100 ms; process-loopback activation wait bounded; watch_free unregisters before freeing and waits for running callbacks; UTF-8/UTF-16 conversions NULL-safe; QueryFullProcessImageNameW buffer 32768; HRESULT mapping (DEVICE_INVALIDATED REOPEN vs LOST, SERVICE_NOT_RUNNING, DEVICE_IN_USE, E_ACCESSDENIED privacy); SetProcessInformation, PowerCreateRequest/PowerSetRequest and timeBeginPeriod usage checked against the docs (WebFetch).

Routing-phase judgement: the shared layer is a sufficient base for per-application capture (process loopback include/exclude tree, agile handler, runtime probe, start-time identity), endpoint loopback ('<id>.monitor', with a 5 ms poll so idle loopback works), capture devices, keep-alive renders, session naming/ducking opt-out, multi-watcher hotplug and friendly names of unplugged endpoints. Missing: the D8/none/virtual locator (finding 1) and the any-rate fallback when AUTOCONVERTPCM is refused (last finding).

Only the user's PC can verify: real render/capture/loopback/process-loopback audio, IAudioClock behaviour during starvation, session-control refcounts, MMCSS/power requests, real unplug/default-device changes, and the DEVICE_IN_USE behaviour with rekordbox.
